source: ដំណាំទុរេន (Durian Cultivation), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, 2015, 31pp
text: Pruning objectives described in this source include maintaining a single strong central trunk with well-spaced main scaffold branches (avoiding narrow branch angles that are structurally weak and prone to splitting under a heavy fruit load), removing dead, diseased, and crossing wood to improve air circulation and light penetration into the canopy, and, on mature bearing trees, controlling canopy height and spread with an eye toward safer and easier harvest access, since durian fruit is heavy and harvested by cutting from above or by hand from a ladder. Cut surfaces from pruning should be treated with a fungicide paste, particularly on larger cuts, to reduce the risk of canker and other fungal infection entering through the wound, matching the disease-prevention guidance given elsewhere in this batch.
